title: kagent-dev/kagent — Cloud Native Agentic AI | Discord:https://bit.ly/kagentdiscord
content:
kagent is a Kubernetes native framework for building AI agents. Kubernetes is the most popular orchestration platform for running workloads, and kagent makes it easy to build, deploy and manage AI agents in Kubernetes. The kagent framework is designed to be easy to understand and use, and to provide a flexible and powerful way to build and manage AI agents.
- Agents: Agents are the main building block of kagent. An Agent is a Kubernetes custom resource that brings together an agent's behavior and runtime configuration.
- Agent Templates: A system prompt, a set of tools and subagents, and an LLM configuration define an agent's behavior. You can define this directly in an Agent or share it across agents using an AgentTemplate resource.
- Harnesses: A Harness defines how an agent runs. Kagent supports its own Go and Python ADKs, Codex, Claude, and custom runtimes, so you can choose the runtime that fits your agent.
- LLM Providers: Kagent supports multiple LLM providers, including OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Vertex AI, Ollama and custom providers and models accessible via AI gateways. Models are configured through the ModelConfig resource, with provider support depending on the chosen Harness.
- MCP Tools: Agents can connect to MCP servers that provide tools. Kagent comes with an MCP server with tools for Kubernetes, Istio, Helm, Argo, Prometheus, Grafana, Cilium, and others. Agents connect through RemoteMCPServer resources, which can be shared across agents.
- Sessions: Sessions keep conversations and task history across interactions. You can suspend and resume an agent, or create a checkpoint and fork a new conversation from it.
- Observability: Kagent supports OpenTelemetry tracing, which allows you to monitor what's happening with your agents and tools.
- Kubernetes Native: Manage agent and tool configuration through Kubernetes APIs and familiar kubectl workflows.
- Extensible: Add custom tools, skills, and runtimes to connect agents to your own systems.
- Flexible: Choose the models and runtimes that fit your workload, and reuse agent templates across compatible harnesses.
- Observable: Trace agent, model, and tool execution with OpenTelemetry and your existing observability stack.
- Declarative: Define agents in YAML, keep configuration in version control, and deploy through GitOps workflows.
- Testable: Test agents through their public APIs and use task history and traces to diagnose failures.
flowchart TD
    UI[UI] --> CONTROLLER[kagent Controller]
    CLI[CLI] --> CONTROLLER
    CONFIG[Kubernetes resources] --> CONTROLLER
    CONTROLLER --> DB[(PostgreSQL)]
    CONTROLLER --> SUBSTRATE[Substrate]
    SUBSTRATE --> RUNTIMES[Agent runtimes]
    CONTROLLER -->|A2A| RUNTIMES
    Kagent brings together the following components:
- Controller: The controller watches kagent custom resources, prepares agents to run, and manages their sessions. It exposes gRPC, A2A, and MCP APIs for clients to interact with agents.
- UI: The UI is a web UI that allows you to manage agents and tools and chat with your agents.
- Agent Runtimes: Agents run using the Go or Python ADK, Codex, Claude, or a custom runtime, selected by their Harness.
- Substrate: Substrate runs the agents and manages their lifecycle, including suspension, resumption, and snapshots.
- PostgreSQL: PostgreSQL stores sessions, tasks, and conversation history so they persist independently of the running agents.
- CLI: The CLI is a command-line tool that allows you to manage agents and tools and interact with your agents.
For more details on the v1 architecture, including resource definitions and how agents run, see the architecture guide.

report.summary: kagent is a CNCF Kubernetes-native framework for building, deploying, and managing AI agents declaratively with flexible runtimes, MCP tools, and observability.
report.background: Kubernetes became the default orchestration platform for cloud workloads, but AI agents are often run as ad hoc scripts or bespoke services without standard deployment, lifecycle management, or observability. As agentic AI moves from demos to production, teams need versioned configuration, repeatable rollouts, and shared tool access. kagent, a Cloud Native Computing Foundation project, applies Kubernetes custom resources and GitOps patterns to agents. It defines agents and templates as CRDs, separates behavior from runtime via harnesses, connects agents to MCP tool servers, and stores sessions in PostgreSQL. A controller exposes gRPC, A2A, and MCP APIs, while a UI and CLI manage agents. This reflects the broader convergence of cloud-native infrastructure and AI agent operations.
key_points: Agents as Kubernetes resources: An Agent is a custom resource combining behavior and runtime configuration; AgentTemplate resources let teams share prompts, tools, subagents, and LLM settings across agents. Because configuration is YAML in version control, teams can use kubectl and GitOps to review, deploy, and roll back agents like any other cloud-native workload.

Flexible harnesses and models: A Harness chooses how an agent runs—kagent’s Go or Python ADKs, Codex, Claude, or custom runtimes. ModelConfig resources configure LLM providers such as OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Vertex AI, Ollama, and gateway-accessible models. This avoids lock-in and lets each workload use the best runtime and model.

MCP tool ecosystem: Agents connect to MCP servers for tools and can use RemoteMCPServer resources shared across agents. Kagent ships an MCP server covering Kubernetes, Istio, Helm, Argo, Prometheus, Grafana, Cilium, and more, enabling agents to inspect and operate cloud-native infrastructure through standardized tool interfaces.

Persistent sessions and observability: Sessions retain conversation and task history; users can suspend, resume, checkpoint, and fork conversations. PostgreSQL stores sessions independently of running agents. OpenTelemetry tracing covers agent, model, and tool execution, and agents can be tested through public APIs and diagnosed with task history and traces.

Controller-centric architecture: A controller watches kagent resources, prepares agents, manages sessions, and exposes gRPC, A2A, and MCP APIs. A web UI and CLI support management and chat, while Substrate runs agents and handles lifecycle, suspension, resumption, and snapshots. This separates the control plane from agent runtime and persistence.
report.impact: kagent signals that agentic AI is being absorbed into cloud-native operations. For the AI industry, it pushes standardized control planes for agents—declarative resources, shared templates, MCP tools, and OpenTelemetry—rather than bespoke frameworks. Developers already using Kubernetes can deploy agents with familiar kubectl and GitOps workflows, mix runtimes and LLM providers, and connect agents to infrastructure tools through MCP servers. That could speed adoption for platform and SRE teams automating Kubernetes, Istio, Argo, and observability tasks. Regular users may not interact with kagent directly, but they benefit indirectly as agent-powered operations become more reliable, auditable, and observable. Challenges remain: Kubernetes complexity, security of agent tool access, and the maturity of a project still in active development.
report.tools: Follow kagent on GitHub and its Discord or CNCF Slack channels. Complementary tools include Kubernetes and kubectl for deployment; Argo CD or Flux for GitOps; Prometheus and Grafana for metrics; OpenTelemetry for tracing; MCP servers for tool integration; Ollama for local models; and kagent’s UI and CLI for managing agents. Teams evaluating agent runtimes can compare kagent’s Go and Python ADKs with Codex, Claude, or custom harnesses, and watch CNCF project progress.
